questions.architecture: Pure core holds. M18.145's REFERENCE_PATHS, referencesUnchanged and lazy checkDiff are pure functions in packages/core with no DOM, timers or randomness. checkDiff, REFERENCE_PATHS and referencesUnchanged are not exported from core's index, so no public API changes (changeset patch). render's connectorText change stays in render. M18.132's catcher is editor-only DOM. M18.180's direct kill is in packages/cli (node side) and changes the OwnedBrowserProcess type internally (immediate removed, kill added on the Playwright process type). There is no contract change, no new runtime dependency and no file-format change. Security: M18.180's SIGKILL ends only the browser's own process, and the argued r1 F1 relies on Chromium's children dying with their parent. M18.190's plan removes it again. The cleanup-failure reporting contract (NFR-SEC-001: report when owned termination fails, never hide it) is what M18.180 broke on Windows (F2).

findings.evidence: Run here at 084008f: 'last-ci: ci green at 6a672da (run 40823582744) (7 newer runs pending)', exit 0. GitHub at the same time: verify (windows-latest) failed in ci 40837280675 (3ffad13, 08:09Z), 40837862173 (ac64e7b, 08:30Z), 40840477206 (453b5ca, 08:35Z), 40849659371 (475402c, 09:55Z) and 40858059983 (084008f, 11:16Z, plus cli-mcp windows node 22/24). The loop reads only the newest completed run. A completed green with any number of newer pending runs prints green: the LAST_CI_MAX_PENDING (4) unknown rule applies only when no run completed (line 148), and failed jobs inside a still-running run are never read. Stream 2's 0024bcc/e06dbd7/453b5ca were pushed 08:01-08:12Z over the previous batch's incomplete runs, against cp22's 'green ci between' order. 453b5ca came 3 min after 3ffad13's Windows job had failed.
findings.failure_scenario: Under a 3-4 h queue, a platform break shows as a failed job long before its run completes. Until then drive/next-task's red-main stop prints green and exits 0, so feature batches keep landing on a red main: cp12's failure mode, now on the 'older green' branch. With M18.178 closed and no mark open, nothing else stops them.
findings.recommendation: Read the jobs of each newer pending ci run: any job concluded failure (not cancelled) is RED at that run (exit 1, or 2 when a declared Fixes-ci for it is pending, as today). Treat more than LAST_CI_MAX_PENDING newer pending runs behind a completed green as UNKNOWN (exit 3). Add harness cases for both, using a runs-file shape that carries jobs.

findings.evidence: plannedCiFix checks only that the task's row is open on the base and that its acceptance text contains the same `Fixes-ci: <id>`. The id is never checked as a failed ci run of the branch. The row can be brought by any commit confined to HARNESS_PATHS, and docs/backlog/ is one, which lands while the mark is open. The exemption holds for every later commit of that task while the row stays open (author's r2 minor). The fix commit may set its own row done while the run stays red (M18.180, done at 084008f, ci 40858059983 red). land.mjs's path has no test (r2 minor).
findings.failure_scenario: While a `blocks-landing` row is open, a reviewed backlog-only commit adds 'M18.x feature ...; the commit SHALL carry `Fixes-ci: 123`' with any number. Any product commits for M18.x then land through the mark. The mark degrades to a self-issued label, which cp15's Learned line says is no gate. Only the per-commit reviewer stands between them.
findings.recommendation: Require the id to be a completed ci run on the branch whose conclusion is failure (land.mjs and CI's check-checkpoint can query it; refuse when unreadable). Make the exemption one-shot: refuse a second commit of the task once one carrying the trailer has landed since the row was added. Add a land.mjs-path test.
